questions.question: Article 1 of the Indian Constitution which states "India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States', mentions which of the following features?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cooperative Federalism.**__

__
 
• **Cooperative Federalism**

 
 
• **​This feature is explicitly mentioned in Article 1 of the Indian Constitution**
 
• It refers to the sharing of power between the central government and the state governments in India
 
• It is a key principle of Indian federalism and is reflected in the division of powers between the Union and the states in the Constitution
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This feature is not explicitly mentioned in Article 1 of the Indian Constitution
 
• However, the Constitution does provide for an independent judiciary in other articles, such as Article 50 which calls for the separation of the judiciary from the executive
 
 
 
• **Secularism**
 
 
• This feature is not explicitly mentioned in Article 1 of the Indian Constitution
 
• However, it is mentioned in the Preamble which declares India to be a secular nation
 
• The Constitution also provides for religious freedom and prohibits discrimination on the basis of religion
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary sovereignty**
 
 
• This feature is not explicitly mentioned in Article 1 of the Indian Constitution
 
• However, it is implied in the Constitution as the Parliament is the supreme law-making body in India
 
• The Constitution also provides for a system of checks and balances to prevent the abuse of parliamentary power

• Panchayati Raj

 
 
• Panchayati Raj is the system of local self-government of villages in rural India as opposed to urban and suburban municipalities.
 
• It consists of the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through which the self-government of villages is realized.
 
• They are tasked with "economic development, strengthening social justice and implementation of Central and State Government Schemes including those 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule."
 
• ​Part IX of the Indian Constitution is the section of the Constitution relating to the Panchayats.

• Zilla Parishad at the District Level
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the Block Level
 
• Gram/Village Panchayat at the Village Level

questions.question: Which of the following is a bulwark of personal freedom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **1** i.e __**Habeas Corpus.**__

 
• A writ is an order issued by the courts for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• Only the Supreme court of India and high courts have the power to issue writs.
 
• The concept of writ was taken from **Britain.**
 
• Supreme court of India issues writs under **article 32.**
 
• High court issues writs under **article 226.**
 
• There are five categories of writs, namely:
 
 
• The writ of habeas corpus.
 
• The writ of prohibition.
 
• The writ of certiorari.
 
• The writ of mandamus.
 
• The writ of quo warranto
 
 
 
• The writ of **habeas corpus** issued by the court to a person who has detained another person, to produce the latter before the court.
 
 
• The word habeas corpus means 'to have the body'.
 
• **It is known as the bulwark of personal freedom.**
 
 
 
• The writ of **prohibition** is issued by a higher court to a lower court to prevent the lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• The writ of** mandamus** is issued by a court to a public official asking him to perform his responsibilities that he has refused to perform.
 
• The writ of **certiorari **is issued by the supreme court or high courts for the reexamination of an action of a lower court.
 
• The writ of **quo warranto** is issued against a person who claims or usurps a public office.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India vests plenary powers in Parliament to legislate on the subject of citizenship?

__
 
• **Article 11** of the Constitution of India vests plenary powers in Parliament to legislate on the subject of citizenship.
 
• This article gives Parliament the authority to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.
 
• It is part of Part II of the Constitution, which deals with the citizenship of individuals at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• Article 11 empowers the Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
 
• This provision ensures that the Parliament has the flexibility to address all issues related to citizenship as and when required.

• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• Part II of the Constitution (Articles 5 to 11) deals with the citizenship of individuals at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• Article 11 gives the Parliament the power to regulate the right of citizenship by law, which allows for necessary amendments and changes to adapt to evolving circumstances.

questions.question: Identify the writ by the virtue of which the Court directs a detained person to be brought before it to examine the legality of his detention.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Habeas Corpus.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Habeas Corpus** is a** Latin term **that means** "you shall have the body."**
 
• It is a legal writ that allows a **detained person to challenge the legality **of their detention and seek release from custody.
 
• The writ of Habeas Corpus is considered a** fundamental safeguard** against **arbitrary detention** and is enshrined in many legal systems around the world, including the United States Constitution.
 
• When a person files a petition for a writ of Habeas Corpus, they are asking a court to order the person or entity holding them in custody to bring them before the court and** justify their detention.**
 
• The court will then** examine the evidence** and determine whether the detention is lawful or not.
 
• The writ of Habeas Corpus can be used in a variety of situations, such as when a person is being held in** jail without trial**, when they are being held by a **foreign government, **or when they are being held by a **private individual or organization.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mandamus** is a writ that orders a government official or agency to perform a **specific duty.**
 
• **Certiorari** is a writ that allows a higher court to** review the decision **of a lower court.
 
• **Quo Warranto **is a writ that challenges a person's** right to hold a particular public office or position.**

questions.question:
Which of the following will be considered normal residents of India?

A) Indians working in foreign embassies in India.

B) Ambassador for India in the rest of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Both Indian citizens working in foreign embassies within India and the Ambassador representing India abroad are classified as** normal residents of India**.
 
• A normal resident in the context of India is defined as an individual who resides or is situated within the country and engages in fundamental economic activities, including earning, spending, and accruing wealth from that location.
 
• Additionally, normal residents possess the right to reside and work within the country without constraints and may qualify for specific entitlements or privileges.
 
• Indian citizens employed in foreign embassies within India are categorized as normal residents due to their citizenship, residence, and economic contributions within India.
 
• Their activities, including earning income and spending, contribute to the Indian economy.
 
• Similarly, the Ambassador representing India in foreign countries is considered a normal resident of India despite being stationed abroad, as their official duties and economic ties remain linked to India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A resident of India refers to an individual who resides within the geographical boundaries of India for a substantial period.
 
• This term encompasses both Indian citizens as well as foreigners who live in India for an extended duration. 
 
• Residents of India typically engage in various economic activities within the country, including earning income, spending money on goods and services, and potentially accumulating wealth.

• Fraternity is at the heart of school, society, and nation.

• Understanding the importance of fraternity or solidarity and the knowledge that we all belong to a large community, a nation, and the globe is also to discover our innate humanity.
 
• It is only when we recognize our interdependence then we are empowered to help build a peaceful nation and a world.
 
• The citizens need to internalize the principles of equality, justice, and liberty to promote fraternity among all, regardless of religious beliefs, and regional and local diversity.
 
 
 
• JUSTICE, social, economic and political:
 
 
• Justice ensures that the freedom of one does not become tyranny for another.
 
• Justice to be truly meaningful needs sharing of power, compassion towards the underprivileged, and empathy towards the disadvantaged.
 
• An education on rights and duties becomes important to ensure a fight for justice.
 
 
 
• LIBERTY of thoughts, expression, belief, faith, and worship:
 
 
• Liberty of thought and action is a fundamental value embedded in our Constitution.
 
• It is the basis for creativity and exploration of new ideas and experiments that can advance social progress.
 
• Respecting the rights of others to liberty of thought and action is the hallmark of a civilized society.
 
• Ensuring that this liberty of thought and action is not used to belittle or diminish the beliefs and status of others is what constitutes a decent society.
 
• Democracy creates an opportunity to pursue one’s chosen ends and respect others’ rights to do so.
 
• In a diverse country like India, exercising freedom with responsibility is a must for ensuring peace in the nation.
 
 
 
• EQUALITY of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all:
 
 
• Equality is another value enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• Freedom and justice remain mere words if equality is not ensured. It implies freedom from exploitation and ensuring opportunities for an individual’s development, irrespective of background, gender, cultural or socio-economic identity, and status.

questions.question: Habeas Corpus is the writ issued by the Court to bring before a court _________.

options.text: a person to perform his legal duty
a tribunal from doing something in excess
a person who occupies a public office

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a person from illegal custody**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Habeas Corpus** is a Latin term meaning "you may have the body." It is a fundamental right guaranteed under Article 32 and Article 226 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This writ is issued to ensure that a person is not detained unlawfully or without proper justification.
 
• The primary purpose of the writ is to safeguard an individual’s liberty from illegal detention or imprisonment.
 
• The Supreme Court or High Courts can issue this writ to bring a person in illegal custody before the court to determine whether the detention is lawful.
 
• This writ is considered a vital tool in protecting the fundamental right to personal liberty under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Types of Writs in India:**

 
 
• **Mandamus:** Issued to compel a public official, government, or lower court to perform a legal duty they have failed to perform.
 
• **Prohibition:** Issued to prevent a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction or acting contrary to the law.
 
• **Certiorari:** Issued to quash an order or decision of a lower court or tribunal that exceeds its jurisdiction.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** Issued to inquire into the legality of a claim to a public office.
 
 
 
• **Article 32:** Known as the "Right to Constitutional Remedies," it empowers individuals to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• **Article 226:** Empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.
 
• **Global Perspective:** Habeas Corpus is recognized internationally and is a cornerstone of legal systems in democratic countries, ensuring protection against unlawful detention.
 
• **Historical Context:** The concept of Habeas Corpus originated in England and was formalized in the Magna Carta (1215) to protect individuals from arbitrary detention by the monarchy.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of India states that the citizen has to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IV A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Part IV A of the Indian Constitution deals with the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• The obligation to defend the country and render national service when called upon is listed under Article 51A.
 
• Article 51A was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.
 
• Fundamental Duties are borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and were inspired by the Japanese Constitution.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• The Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IV A of the Constitution of India.
 
• These duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act:**
 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it introduced.
 
• It was enacted in 1976 during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• Formed in 1976 to recommend the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
 
• Headed by Sardar Swaran Singh, a senior Congress leader and former Union Minister.
 
 
 
• **Non-Justiciability of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the judiciary.
 
• However, they serve as moral obligations for citizens to promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of India.
